what: Every half of every change of this slice, reverted on its own, against the check that has to notice. The rule the issue states is that a check is not done until it reddens for *each* half rather than for the change as a whole — it was written on #101, where a test covering a traffic fix survived the reversal of one of its two halves.
howToReproduce: Apply the mutation to the named file, build, run the named filter, then `git checkout --` the file. The runner used here is .artifacts/mutate.sh, which does exactly that; it is scratch, not shipped.

mutations.edit: creature.Mode is not (CreatureMode.Fighting or CreatureMode.Downed) -> creature.Mode is not CreatureMode.Downed
creature.Mode is not (CreatureMode.Fighting or CreatureMode.Downed) -> creature.Mode is not CreatureMode.Fighting

mutations.half: memory is never written on panic (writing, half 1)
memory is never written on a wound (writing, half 2)
mutations.finding: Green on the first attempt. No check named the second cause, so deleting the write on combat_downed was invisible; A_party_leaves_its_survivors_with_places_they_remember gained Assert.Contains("wound", causes) and the mutation went red. This is the class of hole the rule exists to find.
